Is it safe to use regular superglue on hard to stitch wounds?
I generally use 91% alcohol to clean before the super glue and have used it for years .

Cyanoacrylates (the main components of superglue) have some minor toxicity, but AFAIK it isn't a cumulative poison or a carcinogen, so as long as you don't die within the first day you'll be fine. I believe the hardened form is even less toxic than the liquid form/vapors, so you are quite safe.

Acetone is capable of softening it if you want to get rid of the superglue. However acetone stings like a motherfucker on open wounds. Get 100% acetone if you want to do that.
Cyanoarcylate has a relatively low toxicity despite it's strong smell. You'd have to try pretty hard to actually die from it. It actually is used for sealing wounds sometimes
